headline: 66kg shisha seized in Dhaka: Three arrested for online sales network
summary: The Department of Narcotics Control (DNC) claims this is the largest single seizure of shisha in the country's history.
details: The Department of Narcotics Control (DNC) arrested three individuals, including twin brothers, for operating an online shisha sales network in Dhaka.
A total of 66 kg of shisha, 41 hookahs, 40 kg of charcoal, and five mobile phones were seized during the operation.
The arrested individuals are twin brothers Ahmed Sharifi (34) and Mehdad Sharifi (34), and another man, Md. Maksud Alam (40).
According to the DNC, the twin brothers are born in Bangladesh to Iranian parents who came for business. They allegedly learned the shisha trade in Iran before setting up an online network here.
The operation began after intelligence revealed the brothers were sending shisha parcels via courier services. Two parcels were intercepted in Bashundhara and Malibagh.
Following the leads, the brothers were arrested from a flat in Kalachandpur, Gulshan, where 45.9 kg of shisha and 20 hookahs were found.
Maksud Alam was later arrested from the Vatara area, where officials recovered 18 kg of shisha and 21 hookahs.
The network used Facebook pages to communicate with customers, display products, take orders, and receive payments via mobile financial services.
The DNC is now analyzing a database of customers and distributors found on the seized phones and Facebook pages to identify other members of the network.
caption:
66 kg of shisha seized in a single operation—the largest in Bangladesh's history.

The Department of Narcotics Control (DNC) arrested three individuals, including twin brothers, for operating an online shisha sales network in Dhaka.

A total of 66 kg of shisha, 41 hookahs, 40 kg of charcoal, and five mobile phones were seized during the operation.

The arrested individuals are twin brothers Ahmed Sharifi (34) and Mehdad Sharifi (34), and another man, Md. Maksud Alam (40).

According to the DNC, the twin brothers are born in Bangladesh to Iranian parents who came for business. They allegedly learned the shisha trade in Iran before setting up an online network here.

The operation began after intelligence revealed the brothers were sending shisha parcels via courier services. Two parcels were intercepted in Bashundhara and Malibagh.

Following the leads, the brothers were arrested from a flat in Kalachandpur, Gulshan, where 45.9 kg of shisha and 20 hookahs were found.

Maksud Alam was later arrested from the Vatara area, where officials recovered 18 kg of shisha and 21 hookahs.

The network used Facebook pages to communicate with customers, display products, take orders, and receive payments via mobile financial services.

The DNC is now analyzing a database of customers and distributors found on the seized phones and Facebook pages to identify other members of the network.

headline_marked: Rickshaw puller [[marked as dead in EC records]] for a decade
headline: Rickshaw puller marked as dead in EC records for a decade
summary: Badsha Sheikh, a resident of Faridpur, spent years trying to prove he is alive after his NID was blocked and his name removed from the voter list.
details: Badsha Sheikh, a 52-year-old rickshaw puller from Faridpur, discovered he was listed as deceased in the Election Commission's (EC) database, leading to his National ID (NID) being blocked.
The issue began in 2014, when he found his name missing from the voter list during the national parliamentary elections. He has since been unable to vote in any election.
To resolve the matter, Badsha Sheikh visited the Faridpur District Election Office, where he presented his government-issued NID card and photo.
Election officials requested a certification from the municipality to prove he was alive. He submitted a certification from the Faridpur Municipality on June 23.
The Chief Executive Officer of Faridpur Municipality, Hosain Mohammad Hai Jaki, criticized the EC officials for making citizens suffer due to their own errors.
Faridpur District Election Officer Tarek Ahmed stated that the information has now been corrected through the the Upazila Election Officer, and Badsha Sheikh is no longer listed as dead.
The District Election Officer claimed that the complaints were perhaps being made without a full understanding of the situation.
caption:
Imagine being alive, but the government records say you're dead. For 10 years, a rickshaw puller in Faridpur fought to prove his existence.

Badsha Sheikh, a 52-year-old rickshaw puller from Faridpur, discovered he was listed as deceased in the Election Commission's (EC) database, leading to his National ID (NID) being blocked.

The issue began in 2014, when he found his name missing from the voter list during the national parliamentary elections. He has since been unable to vote in any election.

To resolve the matter, Badsha Sheikh visited the Faridpur District Election Office, where he presented his government-issued NID card and photo.

Election officials requested a certification from the municipality to prove he was alive. He submitted a certification from the Faridpur Municipality on June 23.

The Chief Executive Officer of Faridpur Municipality, Hosain Mohammad Hai Jaki, criticized the EC officials for making citizens suffer due to their own errors.

Faridpur District Election Officer Tarek Ahmed stated that the information has now been corrected through the the Upazila Election Officer, and Badsha Sheikh is no longer listed as dead.

The District Election Officer claimed that the complaints were perhaps being made without a full understanding of the situation.

#Bangladesh #Faridpur #ElectionCommission #HumanRights #NID #News

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo
